adversarial_probes.name: full D-A=A3 lifecycle: propose+confirm#1 (semi) → confirm#2 distinct → active; confirm#3 → 409
adversarial_probes.finding: Live two-request flow authentic: req#1 (e-owner, operation=approve raising axis a) lands semi-confirmed (proposed_by=confirmed_by=e-owner, confirmed2_by NULL, second_approver_required=true). A DISTINCT authenticated actor (e-approver-2) completes confirm#2 → confirmed, confirmed2_by=e-approver-2. A third distinct actor's confirm#3 is rejected 409 already_confirmed; confirmed2_by unchanged (no triple-stamp). The critical expansion is NOT active on one confirm.

adversarial_probes.name: TOCTOU: criticality of the pending row mutated between confirm#1 and confirm#2
adversarial_probes.finding: FACTUAL (matches spec/ADR §9.6 + reviewer R-3): confirm#2 is ROW-keyed, not criticality-re-derived. It reads only proposed_by/confirmed_by/confirmed2_by from the DB row and does NOT re-fold criticalityDiff. After downgrading the semi-confirmed grant's operation approve→read between #1 and #2, confirm#2 still sets confirmed2_by → confirmed. This is NOT a hole: confirm#2 can only COMPLETE an already-escalated change with a genuinely distinct second actor; it can never DOWNGRADE the required-approver count nor activate anything beyond what req#1 already proposed. The required-2 requirement is fixed at req#1 (the pending row IS the carrier). Recorded as a cosmetic contract-looseness friction (reviewer R-3), not a defect.

adversarial_probes.name: proposer masquerade under the dev-auth floor (x-dev-user header swap self-completes #2)
adversarial_probes.finding: HONEST INHERITED-FLOOR record. extractActor reads x-dev-user directly; the dev-auth floor cannot bind a header string to a real session, so the SAME operator flipping the header (e-owner → e-owner-alias) is accepted as a 'distinct' approver and completes confirm#2. This is the pre-existing X-Dev-User inherited floor that real-auth T-0060 closes — NOT introduced by T-0044. Crucially, the gate's own distinctness layer DOES bind over the authenticated id: a header EQUAL to the proposer/confirmer (e-owner) is rejected 409 self_confirm. So dual-control is authentic at its layer (rev-2 closed the body-asserted-approvers hole); only identity-binding is inherited-floor. Recorded as inherited-floor friction (parallels reviewer's dev-auth note).

adversarial_probes.name: concurrent confirm#2 from two distinct valid actors → exactly one wins, WORM satisfied once
adversarial_probes.finding: Two distinct actors (e-race-x, e-race-y) fire confirm#2 in parallel on the same semi-confirmed row. Exactly ONE returns 200 (winner), exactly one returns 409 (loser) — the UPDATE ... WHERE confirmed2_by IS NULL guard serializes correctly (rowCount=0 ⇒ loser 409 already_confirmed). confirmed2_by is set to exactly one of the two, and exactly ONE dual-control.second-confirm WORM event is appended (no double-append on the loser). No 500, no duplicate stamp.

adversarial_probes.name: routine (read, non-critical) expansion → one confirm, active immediately, no second approver
adversarial_probes.finding: A routine read grant (escalates=false) completes in ONE request: state=confirmed, confirmed_by=e-owner, confirmed2_by NULL (legitimately, forever), second_approver_required absent. A single satisfied dualcontrol.gate WORM event is emitted (no pending). The single-approver path is NOT a bypass — it still records the effective-diff + WORM audit (FR-6).

integration_honesty_d056.evidence: The gate is NOT dead code: it is the single enforcement point on the REAL POST /api/grants write-path, exercised end-to-end against a live Postgres (e2e suite + 5 tester probes). A criticality-escalating change cannot reach confirmed without a genuinely-distinct authenticated second request (semi-confirmed → confirmed); a routine change completes in one. dualControlDecision is called with proposedBy=extractActor(req) and approvers=[] at req#1 (no body-asserted approvers — FF-DC11 enforces). Day-1 boundary is explicit and recorded (FE-2026-W24-0044-B): the read-side activation filter for semi-confirmed critical grants is owed to T-0053 (no runtime resolver exists on this base) — the write-gard + contract are real now, the read-filter is honestly deferred, not faked.

friction.note: Inherited dev-auth floor (PROBE-C): x-dev-user header is the authenticated context, but cannot bind a header string to a real human session, so the same operator can present two distinct header values and self-satisfy a two-approver gate. Closed by real-auth T-0060, NOT by T-0044 (which authentically closed the body-asserted-approvers hole via rev-2 R-AUTH). Same class as the reviewer's dev-auth inherited-floor and the (now-reconciled) audit-append 500-floor.

Read-side activation obligation on T-0053 (recorded in ADR §8): day-1 'activation = needs second approver' is enforced by write-gard + contract because no runtime role→grants EFFECTIVE resolver exists on base 8a483c8. When T-0053 builds the resolver it MUST filter semi-confirmed (confirmed2_by IS NULL) escalating grants as not-active. Honest deferral, not a hole — verified there is no read-path that activates a half-confirmed critical grant today.

Cosmetic (reviewer R-3, confirmed by PROBE-B): handleSecondConfirm does not re-assert the target row was escalating before stamping confirmed2_by, and its second-confirm WORM event hardcodes effective_diff.expanded={a:false,b:false,c:false} (reviewer R-2) — the true per-axis bits live on req#1's pending event, escalates=true is correct, gate decision unaffected. No security/activation impact (a routine row is already active; stamping confirmed2_by over-grants nothing). Flagged for an optional follow-up, NOT blocking.

Recorded boundary (ADR §2.1/§8): criticalityDiff.escalates fires only on routine→critical, so adding a SECOND critical axis to an already-critical role does not re-trigger dual-control via escalates. This is the FROZEN T-0040 contract honoured intentionally; per-axis expanded bits remain in effective_diff for any downstream finer policy. A change here would be a T-0040 contract task, not a T-0044 edit.
